MagSafe engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's MagSafe ecosystem covers storefront language. Developer portal, accessory certification, and Connect actually separate magnetic attach behavior from product-page copy:

  • Made for MagSafe / MFi accessory program — certification, magnet array specs, and compliance testing for third-party MagSafe hardware. Controls whether accessories carry official MagSafe branding. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • AccessorySetupKit & ExternalAccessory — pairing flows and accessory communication APIs for snap-on hardware. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains magnetic attach to buyers.
  • Wireless charging stack — Qi coils, power delivery firmware, and charging-state UI in the binary. Your listing may mention MagSafe 充电; wiring charging hardware is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • MagSafe magnet alignment — ring geometry, attach/detach detection, and case-fit tolerances. Configuring magnet behavior is engineering — AppLocale does not touch it.
  • In-app accessory dashboards — battery level, charging speed, wallet slot management, or case color pickers. Listing copy markets those features; building the UI is engineering scope.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of MagSafe capability flags in the binary.

A working MagSafe integration and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe MagSafe attach, charging, wallets, and cases on the product page in zh-Hans, not how you implement AccessorySetupKit pairing or wireless charging firmware in code.

MagSafe-specific vocabulary — what translates differently in zh-Hans

MagSafe accessory listings use terms general localization guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate magnetic attach features — not a literal paste of US marketing:

MagSafe as brand vs 磁吸充电 (magnetic charging)

Apple keeps MagSafe as a product name in Chinese marketing alongside descriptive terms. 磁吸充电 fits when your hero frame shows wireless charging through the MagSafe ring. MagSafe 充电 mirrors Apple's bilingual phrasing on accessory pages. Pick the term buyers recognize on each screenshot frame — a charging animation needs 磁吸充电-friendly phrasing; a wallet mount may use MagSafe 配件 when accurate.

MagSafe 配件 (MagSafe accessories) vs MagSafe 钱包 (MagSafe wallet)

US pages use MagSafe accessories for cases, mounts, and chargers, and MagSafe wallet for card-holder attachments. Chinese App Store copy commonly uses MagSafe 配件 for general accessory lines and MagSafe 钱包 for wallet-specific frames. If your app supports third-party snap-on mounts but not Apple MagSafe wallet hardware, zh-Hans copy should say 兼容 MagSafe 的第三方配件 — not imply you ship Apple-branded wallet modules.

Snap on, attach, and pairing

US pages use Snap on, Attach instantly, or Works with MagSafe for magnetic alignment. Chinese App Store copy commonly uses 磁吸吸附, 一贴即用, or 兼容 MagSafe when your product actually supports snap-on attach. Do not promise official Made for MagSafe badges in listing copy if your accessory only uses generic magnetic mounts without certification.
